replication.target_description: The referenced primary report concerns narrated anticipatory-looking false-belief tasks in 4.5–5.5-year-old children. The assigned description instead requests an EIT-score/oral-narrative-performance relationship; no corresponding target is identified in this report. Reference and outcome description conflict.

notes: Identity verified independently from the supplied text: title Testing the Role of Verbal Narration in Implicit Theory of Mind Tasks, authors Louisa Kulke and Hannes Rakoczy, DOI 10.1080/15248372.2018.1544140, Journal of Cognition and Development, published online 17 Nov 2018. Full primary journal report with Methods, Results, Discussion and References (printed pp. 1–14), not an abstract-only parse. No PDF supplied. Reference/description conflict: this primary report studies Southgate/Senju and Surian/Geraci anticipatory-looking tasks, not an identified EIT-score/oral-narrative-performance test. No defensible target mapping; the page-11 discussion does not resolve the conflict. Candidate author verdict for Southgate/Senju is mixed (only FB1 replicated), but no success value is assigned to the conflicting EIT target. Southgate/Senju candidate tests, not assigned to a target: p. 7 FB1 DLS t(25) = 7.583, p < .001, d = 3.03 (condition n = 26); FB2 DLS t(21) = −1.466, p = .157, d = −0.64 (condition n = 22). P. 8 combined first-saccade binomial p = .388, correct n = 8, incorrect n = 4; separate FB1 p = .125 and FB2 p = 1. Cross-study first-saccade Fisher test p = .045, d = 1.10; cross-study DLS comparisons FB1 p = .537, d = 0.19 and FB2 p = .006, d = 0.93. P. 9 correlations distinguish Southgate/Senju DLS versus Surian/Geraci FB (r(40) = .415, p = .008, d = 0.91) and TB (r(40) = .112, p = .490, d = 0.23). These printed metrics and p values are kept paired and are not converted. P. 11 is discussion and does not identify one critical statistical test.
